question: How does Percival get even with O'Gallagher after he takes all of the boy's fireworks?
gold: He sets them on fire with the teacher sitting on them
final_answer:
Percival sneaks back into the empty schoolroom, lifts the claret case under which O’Gallagher has hidden the confiscated squibs and crackers, and packs additional gunpowder under it—leaving only a tiny, hard-to-notice train in the green baize.  

When O’Gallagher sits back down on the “throne,” Percival lights the train with touchwood, setting off the stored fireworks and powder so that the claret case blasts upward and O’Gallagher is “thrown up to the ceiling” in a cloud of smoke while the crackers and squibs fizz and bang (and the schoolroom catches fire).

"And so it was in attempting to come and see us that you were wounded and nearly murdered?" "Thank God you are here at last," said Mr Vanderwelt, "and that there is now every prospect of a conclusion to the war." "And you won't go to sea any more--will you, Percival?" said Minnie. "They won't give me a ship, Minnie, after having lost the one I commanded; to be unfortunate is to be guilty, in those who have no interest." "I'm very glad to hear it; then you'll remain quietly on shore, and you will come and see us." As I had been rendered feverish by travelling, and my wound was a little angry, as soon as it was dressed for the night, they left me to repose; but that I could not--the form of Minnie haunted me; to sleep was impossible, and I lay thinking of her till day dawned.

question: What happens to complicate the raid?
final_answer: The raid is complicated when the stealth helicopter “Prince 51” starts shuddering and losing stability on approach—drifting sideways, dropping to within about 15 feet of the ground, and kicking up a dust hurricane that creates near-brownout conditions (leading into the crash sequence).
